title: Web Interview Prep
body:
Entry point for web technical interview prep. Each note below is built around analogy → technical term tables, and every row answers the same question: **which machine does this actually happen on?**

## The topics

- [[HTTP Requests]] — the full lifecycle of a request, from JS building it to the response repainting the screen. Methods, URLs, status codes, HTTPS, IP addresses.
- [[REST APIs]] — the restaurant/menu model of a client-server contract. Endpoints, resources, auth, rate limits, pagination, versioning, webhooks.
- [[Cookies and Browser Storage]] — the wristband model. `Set-Cookie`, cookie flags, same-origin policy, CORS, localStorage vs sessionStorage.
- [[Modern JavaScript Concepts]] — the DOM as a stage set. Reflow vs repaint, virtual DOM, debugging, and what happens at build time vs runtime.
- [[Server-Side Technology]] — front-of-house vs back-of-house. The frontend/backend split, Rails MVC, and SQL storage concepts.

## The one framing that ties it all together

The interview-relevant skill isn't reciting syntax — it's being able to point at any piece of logic and say *which machine it runs on*, and *why it has to run there* rather than the other side of the split. A lot of the trickiest questions ([[CORS]], `HttpOnly`, [[Client-Side Rendering]] vs [[Server-Side Rendering]], build time vs runtime) are really just that one question in disguise.

## Highest-value facts across all five notes

- The client chooses the method, URL, and body; the server only chooses how to respond.
- [[CORS]] and the [[Same-Origin Policy]] are enforced by the browser, never by the server.
- Cookies are attached automatically by the browser; [[localStorage]] never is.
- `HttpOnly` protects against [[XSS]]; `SameSite` protects against [[CSRF]].
- Bundling, minification, tree shaking, and transpiling all happen at build time, never in the user's browser.
- Anything on the frontend can be read and modified by the user, so trust must live on the backend.

## Course notes this builds on

COMP 3612 — [[WEB DEVELOPMENT FOR CS]]: [[HTTP]], [[DNS]], [[Cookies]], [[CORS]], [[DOM]], [[Fetch]], [[Asynchronous JS]], [[Express]], [[Node.js]].
